description.en: Go beyond K-Means with density-based clustering (DBSCAN), hierarchical agglomerative clustering, and Gaussian Mixture Models for soft assignments.
description.ta: K-Means-ஐ தாண்டி அடர்த்தி அடிப்படையிலான கிளஸ்டரிங் (DBSCAN), படிநிலை திரட்டு கிளஸ்டரிங், மற்றும் மென்மையான ஒதுக்கீடுகளுக்கான காஸியன் கலவை மாடல்களை கற்றுக்கொள்ளுங்கள்.

story_variants.en:
## Vaathiyaar's Three Strategies

Vaathiyaar reveals three different sorting tables. "K-Means assumes round groups. But what if your groups are crescent-shaped? Or nested? Or you don't even know how many groups there are?"

### DBSCAN (Density-Based)
- No need to specify K!
- Finds clusters of arbitrary shape
- Labels outliers as noise (-1)
- Key params: eps (neighborhood radius), min_samples

### Hierarchical Clustering
- Builds a tree (dendrogram) of merges
- Cut the tree at any height to get different numbers of clusters
- Linkage methods: ward, complete, average, single

### Gaussian Mixture Models (GMM)
- Soft clustering: each point gets a probability of belonging to each cluster
- Can model elliptical clusters (unlike K-Means which assumes spherical)

```python
from sklearn.cluster import DBSCAN, AgglomerativeClustering
from sklearn.mixture import GaussianMixture
from sklearn.datasets import make_moons
import numpy as np

# Non-spherical data
X, y = make_moons(n_samples=300, noise=0.1, random_state=42)

# DBSCAN
db = DBSCAN(eps=0.2, min_samples=5)
db_labels = db.fit_predict(X)
print(f'DBSCAN clusters: {len(set(db_labels)) - (1 if -1 in db_labels else 0)}')
print(f'Noise points: {(db_labels == -1).sum()}')

# Hierarchical
agg = AgglomerativeClustering(n_clusters=2, linkage='ward')
agg_labels = agg.fit_predict(X)

# GMM
gmm = GaussianMixture(n_components=2, random_state=42)
gmm_labels = gmm.fit_predict(X)
print(f'GMM probabilities (first 3): {gmm.predict_proba(X[:3]).round(3)}')
```

Store the labels in km_labels, db_labels and gmm_labels, put each method's adjusted Rand index (ARI) against y_true into a dict called results ({'KMeans': ..., 'DBSCAN': ..., 'GMM': ...}), and print one line per method. practice_challenges.starter_code:
from sklearn.cluster import KMeans, DBSCAN
from sklearn.mixture import GaussianMixture
from sklearn.datasets import make_moons
from sklearn.metrics import adjusted_rand_score

X, y_true = make_moons(n_samples=300, noise=0.1, random_state=42)

# K-Means
km_labels = KMeans(n_clusters=2, random_state=42, n_init=10).fit_predict(X)

# DBSCAN (density-based: follows the curved shapes)
db_labels = DBSCAN(eps=___, min_samples=5).fit_predict(X)

# Gaussian mixture
gmm_labels = GaussianMixture(n_components=___, random_state=42).fit_predict(X)

results = {}
for name, labels in [('KMeans', km_labels), ('DBSCAN', db_labels), ('GMM', gmm_labels)]:
    results[name] = adjusted_rand_score(y_true, labels)
    print(f'{name:12s}: ARI={results[name]:.3f}')
practice_challenges.expected_output:
KMeans      : ARI=0.254
DBSCAN      : ARI=1.000
GMM         : ARI=0.498
practice_challenges.test_code:
from sklearn.metrics import adjusted_rand_score as _ari
assert set(results) == {'KMeans', 'DBSCAN', 'GMM'}, "results must have the keys 'KMeans', 'DBSCAN' and 'GMM'"
for _name, _labels in [('KMeans', km_labels), ('DBSCAN', db_labels), ('GMM', gmm_labels)]:
    assert len(_labels) == len(y_true), f'{_name} must label every point'
    assert abs(results[_name] - _ari(y_true, _labels)) < 1e-9, f"results['{_name}'] must be the ARI of {_name}'s labels"
assert results['DBSCAN'] >= 0.9, 'DBSCAN should recover both moons (ARI close to 1): check eps=0.2 and min_samples=5'
assert results['KMeans'] < 0.7 and results['GMM'] < 0.7, 'KMeans and GMM assume blob-shaped clusters and should not recover the moons'
assert len(set(gmm_labels)) == 2, 'GaussianMixture should use n_components=2'

under_the_hood.summary: DBSCAN grows clusters from dense points, agglomerative clustering merges the two closest groups again and again, and a GMM gives every point a probability per cluster through repeated E and M steps.

steps.title: DBSCAN counts neighbours inside eps
steps.body: For every point DBSCAN counts how many points lie within distance eps. In scikit-learn the point itself counts, so with eps=0.5 and min_samples=4 a point needs 3 other points inside that radius to be a core point. A point that is not core but sits within eps of a core point is a border point; everything else is noise.

steps.title: Clusters grow by chaining core points
steps.body: Start at an unvisited core point, give it a new cluster id, and pull in every neighbour. Each neighbour that is itself a core point adds its own neighbours too, so the cluster spreads along any dense path, even a crescent. Border points join but never spread further. Points never reached keep label -1.

nodes.label: Neighbour is core? add its neighbours too
No more to add: cluster done

steps.title: Agglomerative: merge the closest pair
steps.body: Hierarchical clustering starts with every point as its own cluster and repeatedly merges the two closest clusters. Take points 1, 2, 6, 7, 15 on a line with single linkage: merge {1,2} at distance 1, {6,7} at 1, then {1,2,6,7} at 4 (gap 2 to 6), and finally 15 joins at 8 (gap 7 to 15).

steps.title: The dendrogram records each merge height
steps.body: Each merge is stored with the distance at which it happened, which is the dendrogram. Cutting the tree at height 5 leaves two clusters, {1,2,6,7} and {15}; cutting at 2 leaves three. The linkage rule decides what 'distance between clusters' means: single uses the closest pair, complete the farthest pair, average the mean, and ward the merge that adds least within-cluster variance.

props.caption: Single-linkage merges and their heights; cut at 5 gives 2 clusters

steps.title: GMM E-step: soft responsibilities
steps.body: A Gaussian Mixture Model keeps, for each component k, a weight, a mean and a covariance. In the E-step it scores each point under every component: weight times Gaussian density. If component A scores 0.3 and B scores 0.1, the point's responsibilities are 0.3/0.4 = 0.75 for A and 0.25 for B.

props.caption: Responsibility matrix: rows are points, columns are components A and B

steps.title: GMM M-step: refit from the soft counts
steps.body: Each component's new mean is the responsibility-weighted average of all points, its covariance is the weighted spread, and its weight is the average responsibility. E and M alternate, and the data's log-likelihood never decreases, so the loop stops when it improves by less than tol. predict_proba simply returns the final responsibilities.

under_the_hood.takeaway: Pick by the shape of your groups: DBSCAN for dense blobs of any shape plus noise, hierarchical when you want to choose the number of clusters after seeing the merge tree, and GMM when you need probabilities rather than hard labels.
